articles.title: Supercell set to absorb Merge Mansion as Metacore acquisition nears close
articles.summary: Supercell has formally agreed to buy the last stake in Metacore, the Finnish studio behind the mobile puzzle game Merge Mansion – a game that will now be absorbed into Supercell’s existing portfolio of live mobile titles if there are no hitches.
body: The agreement makes good on plans Supercell first put forward in the spring, when it said it planned to buy the remaining shares of Metacore and add Merge Mansion to its already impressive roster, which includes Hay Day and Clash of Clans. Player-facing services will resume service as normal while the acquisition process moves forward, and Metacore's development team will keep supporting the existing community. In other words, players don’t need to be worried that things may change.

articles.title: September 2026's Movers and Shakers: Savvy Games Group, Supercell, Scopely, King, Moloco and more
articles.summary: To keep you up to date with the latest movers and shakers in the mobile games industry, we've put together a regular roundup of the latest hires, promotions and, in some cases, exits.
body: If you've recently joined a company or bagged a big promotion, or you're an employer that's just made a hire, drop us an email at news@pocketgamer.biz.

Brian Ward is stepping down from his position as Savvy Games Group CEO after half a decade with the company. Since 2021, he has overseen its investments, acquisitions and expansion across games and esports - including the $4.9 billion acquisition of Scopely.
During Ward’s time at the helm, Savvy also came to own geolocation giant Pokémon Go through Scopely, as part of a $3.5bn deal in 2025.

Ward informed staff that the time has come for new leadership. The deputy governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund Turqi Alnowaiser will serve as interim acting CEO of Savvy Games Group until a new leader is found.

articles.title: Lasse Seppänen departs Supercell to form new UK startup
articles.summary: Lasse Seppänen has departed from Supercell after more than seven years with the studio. Having long served in leadership roles at the company, Seppänen has worked as game lead for Hay Day, Boom Beach and Everdale, supported all Helsinki-based teams as head of game production services, and spent his…
body: In that final role, he helped integrate the studio following the acquisition of Beatstar maker Space Ape.

Seppänen said that his departure from Supercell follows "daydreaming" about startups, especially in the context of maturing AI tools and the opportunities they present to small, ambitious teams. He plans to start a new studio in 2027 and expressed a passion for new game IPs.
He also shared excitement around digital card games, "a category that, in this era of AI tooling, offers plenty of room to build entirely new kinds of game experiences".
While Seppänen hasn’t disclosed the specifics of this next endeavour, he has teased more details "when the time is right".

articles.title: Supercell signs deal to acquire Metacore and Merge Mansion
articles.summary: Supercell has revealed that its planned acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion is moving forward, with the deal now signed and expected to close at the end of September. The terms of the transaction will not be disclosed.
body: Once the deal closes, Merge Mansion will join Supercell’s live games portfolio, while the Merge Mansion team will become part of Supercell.
Merge Mansion was developed by a team that pioneered the merge game genre and built a long-term player base around the title.
"As we move into the next phase together with Supercell, I'm excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players," said Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski.
“Supercell's expertise in operating and growing global live games over many years gives Merge Mansion the best possible foundation for long-term success.

articles.title: Supercell’s acquisition of Merge Mansion maker Metacore to be finalised this month
articles.summary: Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month. Financial terms have not been disclosed.
body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.
points: Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month.
